title: response-fabric-playbook-runbooks-and-game-day-scenarios-2025
author: Asha Mehta
content:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines the ‘Response Fabric’ for Redwood Inference: a concise, repeatable set of procedures, runbook templates, communication artifacts, and game-day exercises that teams use to detect, respond to, communicate about, and learn from incidents. It is intended for engineers, SREs, product on-call, and customer success teams involved in operational incidents.

Scope
-----
- Covers incident classification, triage, escalation, runbook usage, handoffs, external and internal communications, postmortem cadence, and game-day scenarios.
- Applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment support flows.
- Excludes non-production development issues (tracked separately by team).

Quick links
-----------
- Primary runbook repository: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Pager rotations: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-rotations
- Status page templates: bottom of this doc (customer comms section)

1) Incident taxonomy and severity definitions
-------------------------------------------
Use the following severity taxonomy across teams. Severity assignments drive page and comm templates, pager escalation, and executive notification.

- S0 (Emergency): Platform down for customers or system-wide data loss. Immediate 24/7 paged response, exec alert within 15 minutes.
- S1 (Critical): Major degradation for a significant portion of customers (e.g., high error rate >10% overall, or >5% for high-priority customers). Paged; page escalation within 30 minutes if unresolved.
- S2 (Major): Noticeable degradation impacting some customers or features (example: increased latency above SLOs for >30 minutes). On-call, but not exec-level.
- S3 (Minor): Degraded non-critical functionality; handled in-business-hours by product/engineering owners.

2) On-call roles, rotation rules, and handoff checklist
------------------------------------------------------
Roles
- Primary: First responder; triage, initial mitigation, and postmortem lead for assigned incident.
- Secondary: Backup for Primary; takes over if Primary unavailable or for escalation.
- Triage Pool: Team of engineers paged for S1/S0 incidents concurrently (for complex systems like routing and serving runtime).
- Incident Commander (IC): Senior SRE or delegated engineer for incidents that require multi-team coordination.

Rotation rules (standard setup)
- Shift length: 1 week (Mon 09:00 UTC – following Mon 09:00 UTC) for primary.
- Overnight and weekend coverage: rotational; on-call handoffs must be done synchronously at shift boundary or via recorded handoff notes.
- Max consecutive weeks: 3 (exceptions require manager approval).
- On-call compensation and time-off: see people-ops policy; book swaps at least 48 hours in advance.

Handoff checklist (to be filled in the on-call channel and in the shift document)
1. Current incidents and statuses with links to incident channels.
2. Active mitigations and owner(s).
3. Known maintenance or scheduled rollouts that could impact pages.
4. Outstanding runbook gaps and open action items.
5. Pager health check: confirm SMS/Phone/Slack routing.

3) Triage and escalation matrix
-------------------------------
Triage steps (first 15 minutes for S0/S1)
1. Acknowledge pager in PagerDuty.
2. Post a single, concise status line to the incident Slack channel: severity, short impact statement, initial hypothesis, who is responding.
3. Collect immediate telemetry: error rates, latency histograms, recent deploys, infra alerts.
4. If S0/S1: escalate to Secondary and notify Incident Commander.

Escalation matrix (simplified)
- Primary -> Secondary (5–15 minutes) -> IC (15–30 minutes) -> Eng Manager / On-call EM (30–60 minutes) -> CTO/Head of SRE (if unresolved after 60 minutes for S0/S1).

4) Runbook template (standardized)
---------------------------------
Every runbook should follow this flat template (store under eng-platform/runbooks):
- title: short name
- owner: team + primary owner (email/handle)
- scope: what the runbook covers and exclusion list
- symptoms: bullet list of observable metrics/logs/alerts that should trigger the runbook
- immediate mitigation steps (numbered)
- safe rollback steps (if applicable)
- escalation points (who to page next)
- related dashboards and queries (links)
- post-incident actions (assignable TODOs)

Example snippet (paste into new runbook):
```
Title: Router high-error-rate (S1)
Owner: infra-routing-team (@infra-routing)
Symptoms:
- error rate > 8% for 5m on /v1/generate across region-us-east-1
- 5xx count spike in serving-runtime metrics
Immediate steps:
1) Verify recent deploys (CI build id).
2) Enable routing circuit-breaker to route to fallback pool.
3) Increase logging level for affected service for 10m.
4) If error persists, scale up pool by +2 nodes.
```

5) Postmortem process and timeline
----------------------------------
Timeliness
- Initial incident memo: within 8 hours of incident start (public/internal brief).
- Draft postmortem: within 72 hours.
- Final postmortem with action items: within 10 business days.

Postmortem template (must be followed)
- Title, incident id, timeline (UTC), severity, impact summary.
- Root cause analysis (with evidence), mitigations applied, permanent fixes, and a blameless language statement.
- Action items with owners and deadlines.
- Metrics showing before/after impact (error-rate, latency, cost delta).

Review & closure
- Postmortems are reviewed by IC, Primary, Product PM, and a representative from Customer Success for customer-facing incidents.
- Action items tracked in the team backlog; closure confirmation required before incident is marked closed.

6) Customer communications: status page and templates
----------------------------------------------------
When to post: For any S0 or S1 incident with measurable customer impact or when multiple customers are affected.

Status page template (short form that we paste into status.redwood.ai or internal status page):
- Title: [Under investigation] Increased error rates for Redwood Hosted API
- Time: 2025-03-11T14:22:00Z
- Impact: Some users are experiencing increased 5xx errors and stream interruptions for text-generation endpoints in us-east-1.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or earlier with new info.
- Contact: support@redwood.ai; status updates will be posted at status.redwood.ai

Customer email / CS announcement (initial)
Subject: Brief outage notice — Redwood Hosted API (us-east-1)
Hi {CustomerName},
We are currently investigating an issue affecting text-generation requests in us-east-1. Our engineering team is actively working on mitigation and we will provide an update within 30 minutes. We apologize for the disruption. If you have critical workloads, please reply with URGENT to this email and we will prioritize.

Customer update (30m)
Subject: Update — Redwood Hosted API (us-east-1)
Summary: We have identified increased error rates tied to a routing change. Mitigation: traffic has been shifted to fallback pool; error rates are trending down but not fully recovered. Estimated recovery: 60 minutes.

Post-incident customer report (final)
Subject: Incident report — Redwood Hosted API (us-east-1) — {date}
Include: timeline of events, root cause summary, customer impact, actions taken, and permanent fixes with ETA, and contact for follow-up.

7) Game-day exercises and scenarios
-----------------------------------
Purpose: validate runbooks, measure time-to-detect/mitigate, and validate cross-team comms.
Frequency: team-level game-day every quarter; cross-org incident simulation annually.

Suggested scenarios (rotate each quarter)
- Scenario A: Sudden 5xx surge in serving runtime caused by a bad quantized model build. Goal: verify rollback, model-swapping runbooks, and TTL cache invalidation.
- Scenario B: Network partition between control-plane and VPC-hosted customer. Goal: verify Private deployment fallback and customer comms.
- Scenario C: Autoscaler misconfiguration causes sustained queueing and increased latency. Goal: scale mitigation and monitor alert noise.

Post-game-day artifacts
- A short list of measurable outcomes: time-to-detect, time-to-mitigate, comms lag, and runbook gaps.
- Create action items and assign owners; include game-day notes in the team retro.

8) Key metrics, SLO triggers, and monitoring checklist
-----------------------------------------------------
SLOs (examples)
| Service area           | SLO (p99 / error)        | Alert threshold | Pager severity |
|------------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Hosted API availability| 99.95% monthly uptime    | <99.9% for 15m  | S1             |
| Token generation latency| p95 < 500ms             | p95 > 800ms for 20m | S2         |
| 5xx error rate         | <0.5% overall           | >2% for 5m      | S1             |

Monitoring checklist for first 10 minutes
- Check the centralized incident dashboard (link).
- Confirm ingestion of logs and metric pipelines (no backfill delays).
- Confirm distributed tracing spans are present for affected requests.
- Validate PagerDuty and Slack bridge are functioning.

9) Ownership, runbook hygiene, and continuous improvement
---------------------------------------------------------
- Each runbook must list an owner and a quarterly review date.
- Runbook hygiene workflow: owners receive quarterly reminders to review and mark runbook as "verified" or "needs update".
- Postmortem action items should have a target date and be tracked to closure in Jira/Asana.

10) Appendix: practical artifacts and CLI snippets
-------------------------------------------------
Slack incident channel starter (paste to #incident-<id>):
```
:rotating_light: Incident S1 — Router high-error-rate
Impact: ~12% 5xx across region-us-east-1
Responders: @oncall-primary, @oncall-secondary, @infra-routing
Initial hypothesis: recent router deploy 2025-03-11T12:05Z
Runbook: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/router-high-error-rate
```

PagerDuty quick-check (example)
- pdcli incidents list --service "Hosted API" --day | head

Status page quick template (markdown)
```
[2025-03-11T14:22Z] We are investigating reports of increased errors for Hosted API in us-east-1. We will update this status in 30 minutes.
```

Customer comms sample (final)
Dear {CustomerName},
We apologize for the disruption you encountered on {date}. Summary: brief one-paragraph. Root cause: concise sentence. Mitigation: actions performed. Permanent fix: description and ETA. If you need a dedicated follow-up, please contact your account rep.

Governance and exceptions
-------------------------
- Exceptions to rotation rules (e.g., extended leave, travel) are handled by manager approval and must be recorded in the rotation calendar.
- For any S0 incident, legal and security must be notified within 2 hours if customer data exposure is suspected.
